chunks: Draw NMOS and PMOS symbols. The question: Draw a PFET/NFET symbol.
A MOSFET is a transistor controlled by a voltage on its gate. Engineers draw it with a standard symbol, and the symbol itself tells you which type it is.
The N-channel (NMOS) and P-channel (PMOS) symbols are almost identical, and the one clue that separates them is the direction of a small arrow.
Picture the symbol as a tiny diagram of the device. A plate on the left is the gate, held apart from the channel by a gap, which stands for the insulating oxide.
The channel is a broken vertical line on the right with drain at the top and source at the bottom.
The arrow points from the P side to the N side (P and N are the two kinds of specially treated silicon). It points in for NMOS and out for PMOS.
NFET on the left (arrow into the channel, drain on top), PFET on the right (arrow out of the channel, source on top).
In both, the body is tied to the source, which creates the drawn body diode. For the NFET it points source to drain, for the PFET drain to source.
Either way it's reverse-biased in normal operation.
Gate (G): the control terminal, insulated from the rest of the device. Drain (D) and source (S): the two ends of the channel that current flows between.
Body (B): the piece of silicon the channel forms in. The arrow sits on this line. Enhancement mode: no channel until you apply gate voltage. A broken channel line shows this.
Body diode: a built-in one-way valve for current (a diode) from source to drain, often drawn on power MOSFETs.
To draw an NMOS in words: a gate line goes to a vertical plate, a small gap follows, then a broken vertical channel line.
The drain leaves the top, the source leaves the bottom, and the body arrow points into the channel.
For a PMOS, point the arrow out, and usually flip it so the source is at the top, toward the supply. That is the whole idea.
"An NFET symbol is a gate plate separated from a broken channel line, drain on top, source on the bottom, and an arrow on the body pointing into the channel.
The PFET is the same with the arrow pointing out, and I flip it so the source is on top at the supply.
The arrow is the body-channel PN junction pointing from P to N, the broken line means enhancement-mode, normally off, and the gap shows the gate is insulated.
Discrete parts also show the body diode from source to drain."
Quick check. On a standard enhancement-mode MOSFET symbol, the arrow on the body points into the channel. What type is it?
